visual_basis: AI-generated visual concepts, not molecular structures

examples.name: NucB
examples.description: Cuts DNA outside bacterial cells, one of the strands that helps hold a biofilm together.

source.title: Dispersal of Biofilms by Secreted, Matrix Degrading, Bacterial DNase
source.evidence: Primary research identifying extracellular NucB DNase and studying matrix-DNA degradation and biofilm dispersal. This is published evidence, not a Sonazyme result.

examples.name: PslG
examples.description: Breaks down Psl, a sticky sugar polymer that helps some bacterial biofilms attach and hold together.

source.title: PslG, a self-produced glycosyl hydrolase, triggers biofilm disassembly by disrupting exopolysaccharide matrix
source.evidence: Primary research reporting purified PslG-mediated Psl degradation and disassembly of Psl-containing biofilms. It does not establish activity against every biofilm or in a cooling loop.

examples.name: PelA hydrolase
examples.description: The cutting domain of PelA targets Pel, another sugar polymer used to build bacterial biofilm matrix.

source.title: Exopolysaccharide biosynthetic glycoside hydrolases can be utilized to disrupt and prevent Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms
source.evidence: Primary research on the isolated PelA hydrolase domain, PelAh, disrupting Pel-dependent biofilms. The example refers to that domain, not full-length PelA.

examples.name: Dispersin B
examples.description: Cuts PNAG, a sticky sugar chain used by several bacteria to build their protective matrix.

source.title: Modeling and biochemical analysis of the activity of antibiofilm agent Dispersin B
source.evidence: Primary biochemical research identifying Dispersin B activity against beta-1,6-linked N-acetylglucosamine polymers. This supports a PNAG-specific example, not a universal antibacterial claim.

examples.name: Alg2A
examples.description: An alginate lyase that breaks down alginate, a gel-like sugar polymer found in some biofilm matrices.

source.title: Characterization of different alginate lyases for dissolving Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms
source.evidence: Primary comparative research reporting biofilm degradation by the polyM/G-active alginate lyases Alg2A and A1-II-prime. Other alginate lyases in the same study were less effective; activity is not assumed for the whole family.
